description: The India Flood Atlas is a set of modelled 1% annual-chance (100-year) flood hazard maps for all 36 Indian states and union territories, produced by NEER as a public-good project and built on open inputs credited on the site (GEDTM30 terrain, ICESat-2 ATL08 and HydroRIVERS). The live map shows flood depth by state, and the atlas summarises exposure: about 79 million of 383 million mapped building footprints lie in the 100-year floodplain, with 14% of the road network and 17% of railway track flooding at 15 cm or more, ranked by district. Coverage is all of India. Licence: not stated for the flood layers (source datasets are listed with their own licences). Basic access is free, with paid tiers. Caveats: NEER states the maps are modelled hazard for awareness and planning only, not official flood maps and not a forecast, and that they cover modelled populated floodplain areas. Simulation uses: flood depths and building, road and rail exposure for hazard exposure screening, emergency planning and climate adaptation of Indian infrastructure. Related records: the Polish flood hazard and risk maps (data-poland-isok-hydroportal-flood-hazard-risk-maps).
